newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL OVERNIGHT REMAINS AT 5.5 PCT ON SRR CUT RUMOUR.
newsitem.headline: KL OVERNIGHT REMAINS AT 5.5 PCT ON SRR CUT RUMOUR.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate remained at 5.5 percent on Thursday amid rumours of a cut in banks' statutory reserve requirement (SRR), dealers said.
But government sources said there was no immediate plan to cut the SRR -- deposits that banks keep interest-free with the central bank.
"The market has been talking about an SRR cut for a while but the rumour was very strong today," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "They are speculating a two percentage point cut."

A recent tightening of market liquidity following a massive intervention by the central bank in the foreign exchange market to defend the ringgit from speculative attack, had prompted speculation that the SRR would be trimmed from its current 13.5 percent level.
The SRR has been raised by two percentage points since the beginning of 1996.
Dealers said a two percentage point cut in the SRR would free up about 6-7 billion ringgit.
Other interbank rates were slightly softer due to the SRR cut rumour.
One-week money was at 6.1 percent against 6.2/4 percent on Wednesday, while one-month rate was at 7.2 percent against 7.25 percent.
Three-month money was steady at 7.4/5 percent.
Dealers said the market was getting tight again as funds which banks borrowed from the central bank in July were starting to mature and leave the system.

Bank Negara has been lending funds, mostly one-month money, over the past month to help ease market tightness and bring interbank rates down, dealers said. Massive intervention by the central bank in the foreign exchange market in June to defend the ringgit from speculative attack had earlier caused a liquidity squeeze in the money market.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange closed lower after a choppy session.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one point at 92.50, or an implied yield of 7.50 percent.
The December contract was down three at 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
